verification.note: All three files exist in the worktree: frontend/src/lib/listingRequest.ts, frontend/src/lib/semanticSearchRequest.ts and frontend/src/lib/addonStatusRequest.ts. The spec Touch points list (docs/specs/mcp-smart-collections.md:193-195) names only frontend/src/lib/smartCollectionEval.ts, api.ts, semanticSearch.ts and addons.ts '(builders and readers moved out)', plus 'a new server io module under frontend/src/lib/' (frontend/src/lib/smartCollectionServerIo.ts, which exists). None of the three browser-shared request modules is named. The claim is factually accurate. Mitigating point: the '(builders and readers moved out)' parenthetical can be read as covering the destination of the moved builders, and addonStatusRequest.ts:1-27 and listingRequest.ts:1-30 contain only request-building and answer-reading code with no server-only imports, so the placement is plausibly within the spirit of the list. The gap is a scope-documentation mismatch, not a behavioural defect. Severity is not set here.

specification_compliance: Touch-point list (spec lines 193-195) does not name listingRequest.ts, semanticSearchRequest.ts or addonStatusRequest.ts; the finding's factual claim holds. Whether this breaches the list depends on reading '(builders and readers moved out)' as covering new destination modules, which is ambiguous.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The spec does not say where moved builders and readers should live beyond the 'new server io module'; the three browser-shared modules fill that gap without a spec entry.
regression_risks: None identified from the touch-point question alone. The new modules are imported by browser code, so later edits to them affect the browser callers listed in I7.
test_coverage: Not assessed beyond existence of the files; this verification covered only the touch-point scope question.
not_verified: The contents of semanticSearchRequest.ts were not read, so I did not check I3 or I7 behaviour in it.
